pages.content:

StudioPeople

Independent since 2014, in Rotterdam.

Request a proposal

Studio

Kataribe Partners is a Rotterdam public-relations studio founded in 2014 by Mireille Dufort to deliver disciplined, named-list press campaigns. Across five specialized industry sectors, our team of twelve replaces generic wire distribution with direct, personal reporter outreach.

Founding and Independent Studio Philosophy

Kataribe Partners was founded in 2014 by Mireille Dufort, who previously worked as an editor at a trade weekly covering the European energy sector. Having spent years on the receiving end of generic mass press releases, Mireille saw how little value untargeted distribution blasts offered to working journalists. She established our studio in Rotterdam to practice a calm, highly targeted approach rooted in trade journalism standards. We believe PR should function as a reliable storytelling conduit between substantive technical enterprises and the specific writers who understand their sector. Rather than broadcasting announcements indiscriminately across commercial news wires, we research each topic thoroughly, verify who currently covers the subject, and pitch reporters individually by name. Over the past decade, this disciplined philosophy has shaped how we operate across our five dedicated industry practice areas.

Sector Desks and Studio Performance

Our studio operates across five specific sectors: climate and energy, health and life sciences, food and consumer, mobility and cities, and software and B2B. In 2025, our team of twelve delivered forty-six coverage weeks for eighteen ongoing retainer clients, maintaining active working dialogues with 312 vetted reporters across our sector lists. Each desk is led by senior team members who understand sector-specific technical jargon, regulatory backgrounds, and current editorial priorities. We operate from our central office at Westersingel 48 in Rotterdam, working Monday through Friday from 09:00 to 17:30 CET, with extended press desk hours from 08:00 to 18:30 CET during active coverage weeks. When prospective clients reach out, we commit to holding a discovery proposal call within two working days and submitting a formal written brief and scope within five working days.

Hannah Lindqvist writes all releases, briefing packs, and plain-language op-eds. Samir Haddad leads media training, rigorously preparing client spokespeople before Thursday interview sessions. Jet van der Berg manages the client desk, coordinating proposal inquiries, onboarding schedules, and the meticulous weekly coverage log.

Stories we can tell

Our practical approach is illustrated in three recent client stories from the past year. For an innovative heat-pump manufacturer based in Ghent, we conducted a standalone launch week for their quieter outdoor unit, pitching twenty-four specialist reporters and arranging nine technical interviews on Thursday. For a clinical research lab in Leiden operating on our monthly retainer, we coordinated an embargoed trial-result announcement supported by a plain-language briefing note for science writers. For an expanding bakery group in Antwerp on a quarterly retainer, we handled targeted regional and culinary media outreach across three neighbourhood store openings, running one concentrated coverage week per launch. In every case, results were grounded in precise research, prepared executives, and completely transparent logging with no promised coverage.

Request a proposal

The coverage week

Our coverage week is a structured five-day process that takes a single corporate announcement from initial press list curation to completed interviews and a transparent results log. Every step is executed by named studio leads using verified media lists and individual outreach.

The Five-Day Campaign Architecture

A coverage week runs across five dedicated working days: Monday through Friday. On Monday, we agree on the precise news angle, and Lucas Brandão builds a curated list of approximately twenty-five journalists actively reporting on the sector. On Tuesday, Hannah Lindqvist drafts the press release and a one-page technical background note, and the formal embargo deadline is established. On Wednesday, our team conducts personal phone calls and individual emails to every reporter on the list, avoiding mass distribution blasts entirely. On Thursday, client spokespeople participate in scheduled press interviews and follow-up briefings with Samir Haddad sitting in to offer real-time support. Finally, on Friday, Jet van der Berg delivers the comprehensive coverage log, followed by a focused thirty-minute debrief call.

Questions we get asked

Five answers about embargoes, silence, interviews, the log and languages.

How are press embargoes agreed upon and managed?

When an announcement requires advance coordination, Hannah Lindqvist establishes a clear embargo time on Tuesday while finalising the draft release and background note. On Wednesday, our outreach to the twenty-five selected sector journalists explicitly specifies the embargo conditions before full materials are shared. This gives writers sufficient time to review complex data, prepare questions, and request Thursday interviews without the pressure of breaking news prematurely. In technical sectors such as climate and life sciences, respect for embargoes allows journalists to write informed, accurate stories rather than rushed summaries. We track which reporters have formally agreed to the embargo terms directly within the campaign log.

What happens if no reporters choose to write about our news?

Kataribe Partners never promises coverage, placements, or specific outlet mentions. While we achieved strong engagement across forty-six coverage weeks in 2025, editorial decisions rest entirely with independent journalists and editors. If reporters decline an angle on Wednesday, we document their precise editorial feedback in Friday's coverage log. Often, a decline reveals valuable intelligence: a reporter may have recently covered a similar topic, might be working on an upcoming sector feature, or may prefer a different data angle. Understanding exactly who passed and why provides actionable direction for future quarterly retainer pitches or upcoming launch weeks.

How are spokesperson interviews conducted on Thursday?

Thursday is reserved exclusively for scheduled one-on-one spokesperson interviews and rapid follow-up inquiries resulting from Wednesday's pitching. Media-training lead Samir Haddad prepares all client executives in advance, ensuring they are comfortable with key messages, technical nuances, and potential difficult questions. During active interviews, Samir sits in on the calls to take detailed notes, assist with factual follow-up points, and observe reporter engagement. Our press desk operates under extended hours from 08:00 to 18:30 CET throughout the week to accommodate early morning newsrooms and late editorial deadlines, ensuring no media inquiry or interview request goes unanswered.

What specific data is included in the Friday coverage log?

On Friday, Jet van der Berg compiles and delivers our definitive coverage log before our scheduled thirty-minute debrief call. The log provides an unvarnished, line-by-line accounting of all twenty-five journalists on the Monday list. For each reporter, we record whether they opened the pitch, who replied, who scheduled an interview, who published or confirmed future publication, and who explicitly passed along with their verbatim feedback. We do not inflate results with automated web clipping estimates or arbitrary publicity values. Clients receive an accurate, permanent record of their actual standing among key trade journalists across their industry sector.

Which languages do you support for press releases and interviews?

Our studio operates across five core working languages: English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, French, and German. While our central office is located in Rotterdam, our international media relations team pitches trade and business publications across Europe and global sector hubs. Hannah Lindqvist prepares releases, executive briefings, and background documentation adapted for these linguistic regions. During Thursday interview sessions, client spokespeople can conduct discussions in their preferred language, supported by our multilingual desk heads. All campaign proposals, retainer agreements, and price lists remain denominated consistently in EUR excluding VAT, regardless of the campaign language or geographical media market targeted.

Request a proposal

Which brief suits us

We provide straightforward, predictable public-relations retainers designed around structured coverage weeks rather than vague monthly billable hours. All fees are denominated in EUR excluding VAT, with transparent scopes and fixed three-month commitments.

We tailor our public-relations engagements to nine distinct news briefs: product launches, funding rounds, research reports, new site or office openings, founder profiles, expert commentary, trade-show weeks, commercial partnerships, and quiet periods. An intensive moment like a product launch or funding round generally calls for a dedicated standalone Launch week or an ongoing Monthly retainer. In contrast, organisations managing steady operational growth or neighbourhood expansions, such as our bakery group in Antwerp, benefit from a Quarterly retainer. During quiet periods, our Monthly retainer allows clients to stay visible through one quarterly sector-briefing pitch, ensuring their research and leadership remain on the radar of our 312 sector journalists.

Retainer Tiers and Service Specifications

We offer six clearly defined engagement options to fit varying operational cycles. The Brief session is completely free, comprising a sixty-minute discovery call followed by a written brief and proposal within five working days. The Quarterly retainer costs 2,400 EUR per month and includes one full coverage week each quarter along with an honest coverage log, subject to a three-month minimum. The Monthly retainer is priced at 4,600 EUR per month, delivering one coverage week every month plus one sector-briefing pitch per quarter. For demanding communications agendas, our Sector programme costs 7,900 EUR per month, providing two coverage weeks monthly, spokesperson preparation, and a monthly reporter round-table. For standalone announcements, the Launch week offers a single coverage week for a one-off fee of 6,200 EUR without ongoing retainer commitments. Dedicated Media training is available at 1,800 EUR per session.

Engagement Terms, Notice Periods, and Commitments

All ongoing retainers at Kataribe Partners are contracted on fixed three-month terms. Either party may end the agreement by giving thirty days' written notice before the current three-month term closes. All fees are quoted in EUR excluding VAT, with no hidden administration expenses or unexpected disbursements. We never promise coverage, placements, or specific publication outlets, as editorial discretion belongs strictly to reporters. Our firm commitment is operational: a verified named list of about twenty-five journalists, personal outreach via individual calls and emails, prepared spokespeople, and an exhaustive Friday log. When you request a proposal, we schedule a call within two working days and deliver our written brief within five working days.

Media training sessions cost 1,800 EUR per session and are led by Samir Haddad at our Rotterdam studio or client offices. Each half-day intensive accommodates up to three corporate spokespeople, focusing on practical message discipline, handling challenging interview scenarios, and bridging back to core technical facts. Sessions include recorded mock interviews with realistic follow-up questioning, followed by immediate constructive review. This preparation ensures company leaders enter Thursday interview sessions during active coverage weeks with confidence and clarity. In 2025, prepared spokespeople across forty-six coverage weeks consistently delivered more coherent, authoritative briefings to sector reporters, directly improving the quality of resulting editorial discussions.

Coverage Notes

Coverage Notes is our monthly one-page briefing on European trade media developments and studio campaign availability. Delivered once a month, it provides concise intelligence directly from our five sector desks.

A Concise Monthly Intelligence Dispatch

Coverage Notes is designed for founders, communications directors, and sector executives who want a clear view of trade media without commercial noise. Published once a month by Kataribe Partners, each issue is restricted to a single concise page. The briefing outlines the specific topics, regulatory deadlines, and technology shifts that our five sector desks—climate and energy, health and life sciences, food and consumer, mobility and cities, and software and B2B—are watching. Written by our practice leads, it distils emerging editorial themes and notable changes across trade newsrooms, drawing upon ongoing daily dialogues with the 312 reporters maintained across our proprietary media databases.

Open Coverage Weeks and 2027 Retainer Waitlist

In addition to editorial trends, each issue of Coverage Notes provides a candid status report on our studio capacity. Because we limit our workload to maintain intensive personal pitching—running forty-six coverage weeks across eighteen retainer clients in 2025—we maintain a strict cap on active campaigns. The newsletter lists which specific coverage weeks remain open in the upcoming quarter and manages the waitlist for 2027 retainer places. Organisations planning major product launches, funding announcements, or corporate milestones use this monthly schedule to reserve their campaign slots well before their desired news dates.

This privacy policy outlines how Kataribe Partners collects, manages, and protects business information and personal data. We operate with strict confidentiality and professional trade journalism integrity.

Data Collection and Processing Scope

Kataribe Partners, located at Westersingel 48, 3014 GT Rotterdam, Netherlands, acts as the data controller for personal and business information gathered through this website. We collect only the data necessary to provide professional public-relations services, including contact information submitted through our proposal request forms, email correspondence sent to hello@kataribe.example, and email addresses registered for our monthly Coverage Notes dispatch. Confidentiality and Media List Security

We treat all client corporate announcements, embargoed scientific data, and technical materials with rigorous professional confidentiality. Our proprietary press database of 312 industry journalists is maintained independently by Lucas Brandão in full compliance with European data protection regulations. We never sell, exchange, or publicly expose reporter contact details, nor do we disclose client coverage logs to external third parties.

These terms govern all public-relations engagements, retainer contracts, and advisory services provided by Kataribe Partners. Our working agreements are founded on transparent fixed pricing, defined three-month cycles, and honest operational deliverables.

Retainer Structure and Termination Notice

All ongoing public-relations retainers with Kataribe Partners are established on fixed three-month terms. Either party may terminate an ongoing agreement by providing thirty days' written notice before the conclusion of the current three-month term. For prospective clients, our initial sixty-minute brief session is free, with a formal proposal submitted within five working days of the discussion. Schedule of Fees and Payment Terms

All fees are billed in EUR and exclude VAT across all operational languages and international markets. Our Brief session is free of charge. Ongoing services include the Quarterly retainer at 2,400 EUR per month with a three-month minimum commitment, the Monthly retainer at 4,600 EUR per month, and the Sector programme at 7,900 EUR per month. Scope of Services and Coverage Policy

Kataribe Partners operates strictly as an independent communications advisory studio. We explicitly make no promise of editorial coverage, placements, specific headline inclusions, or publication dates in any print, broadcast, or digital outlet. Independent editorial discretion resides solely with journalists and editors. Our contractual promise encompasses disciplined professional execution: developing a verified press list of approximately twenty-five named sector journalists, crafting high-calibre briefing materials, conducting direct personal outreach by telephone and email, preparing spokespeople, and delivering an exhaustive Friday coverage log accompanied by a thirty-minute debrief call. We never distribute anonymous mass wire blasts.

posts.title: A launch week for a quieter heat pump
posts.excerpt: How a concentrated five-day coverage week in Ghent introduced a quieter outdoor heat-pump unit to twenty-four sector reporters and resulted in nine technical interviews.
posts.content:
A heating equipment manufacturer based in Ghent had spent eighteen months re-engineering the outdoor compressor of their residential air-to-water heat pump. The resulting unit operated at a sound pressure level significantly lower than comparable market models, resolving one of the primary planning and neighbour dispute objections facing suburban heat-pump installations. When the engineering team prepared to launch the unit across Northwestern Europe, they sought to avoid the generic fanfare of commercial wire distributions. They came to Kataribe Partners to execute a standalone Launch week—our fixed 6,200 EUR campaign structure—focused exclusively on reaching journalists who report on climate technology, building services, and residential energy transitions.

The campaign began on Monday with Lucas Brandão building a dedicated press list of twenty-four journalists. Rather than assembling a sprawling, indiscriminate database of hundreds of generic regional contacts, Lucas identified the specific reporters across trade publications, architecture journals, and clean-energy desks who regularly review HVAC hardware and decarbonisation policies. In our Rotterdam studio, managing partner Mireille Dufort, who leads our climate and energy desk, aligned the technical angle with the client's leadership. The focus was kept strictly on acoustic engineering data and installation compliance rather than vague corporate sustainability claims.

On Tuesday, Hannah Lindqvist drafted the formal press release along with a concise one-page technical background note. The briefing sheet outlined the decibel measurements, acoustic laboratory testing methods, and compressor vibration dampening mechanisms in clear, objective language that an engineering editor could immediately verify. An embargo deadline was set for Thursday morning at 06:00 CET, providing recipients with ample time to review the technical specifications. On Wednesday morning, our outreach commenced. There were no automated distribution blasts or blind email merges. Instead, Mireille and our desk team conducted individual phone calls and personalised emails to each of the twenty-four journalists on Lucas's list, briefly explaining why the acoustic data was relevant to their upcoming editorial schedules.

The response from trade writers was immediate and substantive. Because the outreach respected their professional beats and provided verified test figures upfront, twelve reporters requested access to the embargoed background sheet within hours. By Wednesday evening, Samir Haddad had prepared the client's chief acoustic engineer and managing director for incoming media inquiries. Samir led a targeted preparation session, reviewing likely technical questions regarding seasonal coefficient of performance, low-temperature noise spikes, and municipal sound ordinances. When the embargo lifted on Thursday, our Rotterdam press desk managed nine one-on-one technical interviews throughout the day, with Samir sitting in on each discussion to support the spokespeople.

On Friday morning, Jet van der Berg compiled the campaign's definitive coverage log before our scheduled thirty-minute debrief call with the Ghent management team. The log provided an unvarnished, line-by-line breakdown of all twenty-four targeted journalists. Nine had conducted in-depth interviews on Thursday; four confirmed they were scheduling coverage for their upcoming monthly print editions; five passed due to editorial focus on commercial rather than residential systems; and six did not respond. By replacing speculative media promises with disciplined preparation, transparent logging, and direct respect for working reporters, the Ghent launch demonstrated the lasting commercial value of an honest coverage week.
